question: Who found an empirical relationship between the half-life of alpha decay and the energy of the emitted alpha particles in 1911?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Geiger and Nuttall.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geiger and Nuttall found the empirical relationship between the half-life of alpha decay and the energy of the emitted alpha particles in 1911.**
 
• This relationship is known as the Geiger-Nuttall law, which states that the logarithm of the half-life of an alpha decay is proportional to the reciprocal of the square root of the energy of the alpha particle.
 
• **Chadwick and Lawrence discovered the neutron in 1932, which was a significant breakthrough in nuclear physics.**
 
• Fermi and Meitner were instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission in 1938.
 
• **Soddy and Aston made important contributions to the development of the theory of isotopes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chadwick and Lawrence's discovery of the neutron was crucial for understanding the structure of the** atomic nucleus** and paved the way for the development of **nuclear weapons.**

 
 
• **A subatomic particle with a neutral charge and a mass somewhat larger than a proton is called a neutron.**
 
 
 
• Fermi and Meitner's discovery of nuclear fission was a major breakthrough that led to the development of **nuclear energy** and nuclear weapons.
 
 
• **Nuclear fission is the process by which an atom's nucleus breaks into lighter nuclei via a .nuclear reaction**
 
 
 
• Soddy and Aston's work on isotopes helped to establish the concept of atomic number and laid the foundation for modern nuclear physics.
 
 
• **Isotopes are atoms that have the same number of protons but differ in the number of neutrons.**
